speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for your cooperation. To better understand your neck swelling, how long has it been present, and have you noticed any pain or changes in size?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your history of colon cancer and this persistent, painless neck mass, have you experienced any night sweats, unintentional weight loss, or difficulty swallowing? I also need to see the area: REQUEST IMAGES: Neck_ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text: The ultrasound will help determine if this is a metastatic deposit from your colon cancer or a thyroid issue. While we await those images, have you noticed any hoarseness, a lump in your armpit, or any changes in your bowel habits recently?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Colon cancer (colectomy performed), type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, osteoarthritis of the left knee. Social history: Works as a traffic warden, frequently plays golf.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic Colon Cancer to the Neck (Cervical Lymph Node Metastasis).
